issue_context.title: System.ArgumentException: 'overlapped' was not allocated by this ThreadPoolBoundHandle instance.
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Reported offline by an internal partner. They see this error show up frequently and randomly.
![bd189623-4f90-4dc8-88c7-8da7502f6101](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1821173/216673646-af7f6a0b-ac31-4a1e-a8f9-fe39239c0877.jpg)

The relevant code is here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/6a547f269de700cfe333946e1fd744e4332a904a/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/AsyncAcceptContext.cs#L161-L174



### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Exceptions (if any)

System.ArgumentException: 'overlapped' was not allocated by this ThreadPoolBoundHandle instance. (Parameter 'overlapped') at System.Threading.ThreadPoolBoundHandle.FreeNativeOverlapped(NativeOverlapped* overlapped) at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.AsyncAcceptContext.AllocateNativeRequest(Nullable`1 size, UInt64 requestId) at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.AsyncAcceptContext.AcceptAsync() at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.MessagePump.ProcessRequestsWorker()

### .NET Version

(need to verify with the customer)

### Anything else?

The only similar report I see is https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/48402 on the client side.
comments: I'm sure there's an issue here. That code is called from 3 places in a non-linear flow.  Lets try to get a repro from the customer.

Hitting that specific error is weird though, there's only one BoundHandle for the entire server. I don't know how you'd ever end up with a different one in that field.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3ced9681d9eda35cee4c580066ecb3c10a569a1f/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/ThreadPoolBoundHandle.cs#L226-L229
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3ced9681d9eda35cee4c580066ecb3c10a569a1f/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/ThreadPoolBoundHandle.cs#L272-L273
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3ced9681d9eda35cee4c580066ecb3c10a569a1f/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/ThreadPoolBoundHandleOverlapped.cs#L48-L49

Maybe it's null due to a double free?

> Maybe it's null due to a double free?

That's what I was thinking.
We should see if we can reproduce this. I'm assuming this is a first-chance exception?
@mgravell Can you please look into this when you have some time?

agree that `null` seems the most credible scenario; the *only* thing that assigns `null` (or indeed any value other than `this`) is `PreAllocatedOverlapped.OnFinalRelease`, via `PreAllocatedOverlapped.Release` thru `DeferredDisposableLifetime<PreAllocatedOverlapped>`, and that path is called only from:

1. `FreeNativeOverlapped`
2. `AllocateNativeOverlapped` in the exception case (to compensate for the earlier `AddRef`)

Hypothesis: in `AllocateNativeRequest` (via `AsyncAcceptContext.AcceptAsync` via `HttpSysListener.AcceptAsync`) we currently aren't setting `_overlapped` to `null` after freeing it and before creating a new request ; if anything faults and we retry, we'll *do that again next time*, causing this scenario.

Checking `MessagePump.AcceptLoop.ExecuteAsync`, we do indeed `catch` and `continue` (retry) in the fault scenario, which means this is a possible cause.

I'm not sure if we will manage to repro (I'll see what I can do), but my suggestion [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0588658400c1531c89f830cfaf39fa99568103f1/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/AsyncAcceptContext.cs#L167-L170):

``` c#
167        if (_overlapped != null)
168        {
169            boundHandle.FreeNativeOverlapped(_overlapped);
+++            _overlapped = null;
170        }
```

Thoughts?

Assuming this is the cause and makes the multiple release problem go away, there are then two possible outcomes I can see:

1. if the fault was transient, we report the correct/underlying fault briefly then continue working
2. if the fault was terminal, we report the correct/underlying fault and stop working

either way, at least the correct/underlying fault is visible
[PR with proposed tweak](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/46504); I'll see if I can think of any way to prove it!

The more I think about this, the more I'm thinking "concurrency, overlapped accepts". I'll try to run some overlapped scenarios through. It is sort of weird that we free something simply because we're about to start a new one, rather than because the old one reached a closing state, but that might just be my learning curve!
I think the issue there is that the Accept object is using a buffer that then gets handed off to the request, or wasn't big enough so we need to try again with a bigger one.
@mgravell @Tratcher is there update on this issue? We are seeing continuous repro'es in our internal service.
Possibly. This may be related to (or identical to) a similar glitch/symptom that we have been investigating internally, and hope to have a resolution in place soon.

> This should be fixed now.

Thanks @BrennanConroy! Would you mind tagging in what release it has been fixed?
Looks like the fix is [in the 8.0.8 service branch](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/tree/v8.0.8/src/Servers/HttpSys); so: I *believe* 8.0.8, which was released 2024-08-15

review_comments:
So the theory is that this or the next line is throwing before _overlapped gets overridden? I agree that CreateRequestContext doesn't seem like something that's super likely to throw. Maybe we could force it by using a test HttpSysListener.MemoryPool that throws from Rent(). 

It still doesn't make sense to me that throwing from AllocateNativeRequest is the cause of the issue though. The customer observed the ArgumentException being thrown from this method, so why wouldn't the customer observe the first exception that led to the later ArgumentException being thrown from the same method?

Any non-shutdown exception would lead to an error-level "Failed to accept a request." log, right? Did the partner reporting this see anything like this @Tratcher? And did we verify that double-freeing the overlapped handle causes a ArgumentException with the "'overlapped' was not allocated by this ThreadPoolBoundHandle instance." message?

AllocateNativeOverlapped throwing an OOM might be more plausible than CreateRequestContext throwing, but we could throw from Rent() to verify that throwing from one of these lines could lead to just the ArgumentException being observed without the original exception being observed for some reason.

The other idea I'm still looking into is a race related to the timing of this release; I need to familiarise myself with how this counter is meant to work, i.e. why we're releasing it *now*, rather than on the way out of a handled request (or both, as long as we added appropriately). I also wonder whether some obscure race meaning it doesn't get incr'd fast enough might cause this, i.e. we decr'd before it got incr'd, but: still digging.
